record.title: ProgramDistill reports a reference-guided benchmark where coding-agent success falls as web-app restoration depth grows
record.summary: The arXiv v1 paper introduces ProgramDistill, a benchmark built from 26 interactive web applications. Its automated pipeline reports 1,975 replay-verified behaviors and 4,063 repair tasks. On the paper’s nine-agent partial-application evaluation, success on two leading agents falls as restoration depth grows from 1 to 8: GPT-6 Astra from 100% to 64.0%, and Claude Opus 5 from 96% to 32%. The authors report that this decline persists among runs with similar prompt lengths. These are author-run benchmark results; the benchmark was not independently reproduced and the authors say its public release is still in preparation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors introduce ProgramDistill, which derives replayable software-engineering tasks from interactive reference applications by mining behaviors, masking their implementations and measuring whether agents restore them.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that mine–craft–patch generated 1,975 replay-verified behaviors and 4,063 tasks across 26 web applications; they state that the public benchmark release is still in preparation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In partial-application reconstruction, the paper reports GPT-6 Astra success declining from 100% at restoration depth 1 to 64.0% at depth 8, and Claude Opus 5 declining from 96% to 32%. The authors report that a similar decline persists within comparable prompt-length bands.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On full-application reconstruction, the authors report mean cumulative-workflow recovery of 49.15% for GPT-6 Astra, 28.81% for Claude Opus 5, and 21.07% for GPT-5.6 Sol across their 12-app evaluation.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish independent reproduction or that the benchmark results transfer to other application classes, production coding tasks, or different agent harnesses.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of benchmark construction or model evaluations was conducted.
The paper reports results on 26 web applications and selected agent harnesses; transfer to other software domains and production workflows is unknown.
The paper compares selected frontier coding agents but does not establish that the restoration-depth effect is invariant to agent harness and observation-budget choices.

brief.importance_rationale: If the benchmark and depth effect generalize, evaluation of coding agents would need to measure behavior inference and cumulative repair from reference applications, not only issue-specified tasks. This could affect agent selection and training, but the evidence is one paper and a bounded web-app testbed.
limitations: Single arXiv v1 preprint; no independent reproduction was conducted.
The task corpus contains 26 interactive web applications, including OSWorld-derived applications and open-source projects or SaaS clones; this is not a broad sample of all software engineering.
The benchmark pipeline uses GPT-5.6 Sol for task construction; construction-model choices may shape the task distribution.
The paper reports nine agent configurations and selected harness/settings; effects may change with tools, observation budgets or model versions.
The authors state that the public benchmark release is still in preparation.
Success is replay-based behavioral recovery; it does not directly measure code quality, maintainability, user value or production safety.
brief.summary: The arXiv v1 paper introduces ProgramDistill, a benchmark built from 26 interactive web applications. Its automated pipeline reports 1,975 replay-verified behaviors and 4,063 repair tasks. On the paper’s nine-agent partial-application evaluation, success on two leading agents falls as restoration depth grows from 1 to 8: GPT-6 Astra from 100% to 64.0%, and Claude Opus 5 from 96% to 32%. The authors report that this decline persists among runs with similar prompt lengths. These are author-run benchmark results; the benchmark was not independently reproduced and the authors say its public release is still in preparation.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report that coding-agent success falls with restoration depth on partial-application reconstruction and that full-app recovery remains low even for the strongest tested agent. These findings are bounded to their replay-verified web-application tasks.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper includes model-cost and execution-time appendices, but no normalized cost-adjusted outcome is summarized here; inference cost is not needed to support the bounded restoration-depth claim.
technical.demonstrated_result: Direct inspection confirms that arXiv v1 specifies the benchmark method and reports the stated task counts and outcomes. The empirical results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.
technical.implementation_status: The paper says the public benchmark release is in preparation. This activation inspected the preprint HTML but did not access code or task artifacts.
technical.mechanism: The mine–craft–patch pipeline discovers user-visible behaviors in a working reference application, replays them to verify traces, masks source implementations to create repair tasks, then checks whether a coding agent restores the reference behavior. Prerequisite lineages control restoration depth.
technical.regime: The benchmark spans 26 web applications and 4,063 tasks. The paper reports nine frontier coding agents; task-construction stages use GPT-5.6 Sol. Selected performance results compare GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. Full-app results cover 12 applications.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes replay validation and pinned application instances, but the task artifacts and scripts were not independently retrieved or run. Independent reproduction remains open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within benchmark tasks, agents are compared using shared replay-verified behaviors and reference/current application setup. No independent benchmark or matched alternate-harness replication was inspected.

brief.title: ProgramDistill reports a reference-guided benchmark where coding-agent success falls as web-app restoration depth grows
brief.why_it_matters: The benchmark tests a coding-agent demand that issue-based tasks often omit: infer behavior from a working application, then restore it in a partial implementation. If its replay verification and depth controls generalize, it could help distinguish agents’ information gathering and multi-step repair ability. The evidence is confined to the paper’s web applications and experimental harness.
